card.name: Words just before money is received
card.fires_on: The word "paid", "pay" or a nearby word like "to" or "their" where the next word would be a payment, royalty or income. It appears in passages about royalties, wages, leases and trust income.

modes.label: Paid to a recipient
modes.description: The word "paid" or "pay" just before a royalty or fee goes to someone.
modes.example: The royalty was to be based on the market value at the place of production, and was to be<< paid>> to the National Treasurer of the Osage

modes.label: Words leading into receiving money
modes.description: A small word such as "to", "I" or "their" where the text is about to name money or income received.
modes.example: By the terms of the contract with Foster, the Osages were<< to>> receive one-tenth royalty (later changed

card.writes: It pushes up support-type words and pushes down money words like earnings, income and profits.
card.plain: It fires on words that set up a payment about to be made or received, such as "paid" before a royalty.
